summary.headline: Loss-making, with negative equity and heavy short-term debt: the price assumes a rescue
summary.text: LAUGFS Gas PLC (LGL.N0000 voting, LGL.X0000 non-voting) runs Sri Lanka's second LPG brand, plus LPG ships, a Hambantota terminal and a Dubai trading arm. The home LPG business still makes an operating profit (Rs 2.1bn in the year to March 2026), but the shipping and trading arms lost Rs 3.6bn, so the group lost Rs 3.34bn (EPS minus Rs 8.64) and another Rs 578mn in April–June 2026. It has lost money in five of the last six years, owes about Rs 36.9bn (Rs 20.3bn of it due within a year) against Rs 3.2bn of cash, and shareholders' equity is now negative (NAV minus Rs 4.97 a share). Even so, the share roughly doubled in a year to Rs 51 (voting, end of June; check the live price), valuing the equity at about Rs 19bn. On a sum of the parts, after debt, I get a fair value of about Rs 7.90, and nil in the bear case. I'd only buy at up to about Rs 6.70 (strong buy under Rs 5.90), and would avoid it until the debt is dealt with.

highlights.title: Three months to 30 June 2026 (unaudited)
highlights.text: Group revenue halved to Rs 6.04bn because the Dubai trading arm had no outside sales. The loss to owners widened to Rs 578mn (EPS minus Rs 1.49 against minus Rs 0.82). The LPG business's operating profit fell to Rs 124mn from Rs 510mn as margins narrowed.

highlights.title: Year to March 2026 (per the fourth-quarter report)
highlights.text: Loss to owners Rs 3.34bn (EPS minus Rs 8.64). The LPG business made Rs 2.11bn of operating profit and Rs 183mn after interest and tax; shipping lost Rs 2.52bn and trading Rs 1.08bn. The audited 2025/26 annual report isn't in the folder yet.

highlights.title: Debt and negative equity
highlights.text: Borrowings rose to Rs 36.9bn at June 2026 (Rs 20.3bn short-term) against Rs 3.2bn of cash. Equity to owners is minus Rs 1.92bn. Finance costs were Rs 2.8bn last year, more than the whole group's operating profit.

highlights.title: The share price
highlights.text: The voting share rose from Rs 26.70 to Rs 51.00 in the year to June 2026 (it touched Rs 80 in January–March 2026) despite the losses. LAUGFS Holdings owns 74% of the voting shares.

fullText:
Summary: LAUGFS Gas PLC (LGL.N0000 voting, LGL.X0000 non-voting) runs Sri Lanka's second LPG brand, plus LPG ships, a Hambantota terminal and a Dubai trading arm. The home LPG business still makes an operating profit (Rs 2.1bn in the year to March 2026), but the shipping and trading arms lost Rs 3.6bn, so the group lost Rs 3.34bn (EPS minus Rs 8.64) and another Rs 578mn in April–June 2026. It has lost money in five of the last six years, owes about Rs 36.9bn (Rs 20.3bn of it due within a year) against Rs 3.2bn of cash, and shareholders' equity is now negative (NAV minus Rs 4.97 a share). Even so, the share roughly doubled in a year to Rs 51 (voting, end of June; check the live price), valuing the equity at about Rs 19bn. On a sum of the parts, after debt, I get a fair value of about Rs 7.90, and nil in the bear case. I'd only buy at up to about Rs 6.70 (strong buy under Rs 5.90), and would avoid it until the debt is dealt with.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 51.00 voting, Rs 42.10 non-voting (last traded, 30 June 2026). Please check them live. In April–June 2026 the voting share traded between Rs 50 and Rs 68; a year earlier it was Rs 26.70.
Three months to 30 June 2026 (unaudited): group revenue Rs 6.04bn (Rs 12.06bn), operating profit Rs 93mn (Rs 525mn), finance costs Rs 662mn, loss to owners Rs 578mn, EPS minus Rs 1.49 (minus Rs 0.82). The Sri Lankan LPG business: revenue Rs 6.01bn (flat), operating profit Rs 124mn (Rs 510mn), loss Rs 234mn.
Year to March 2026 (fourth-quarter report): group revenue Rs 37.24bn (down 16%), loss to owners Rs 3.34bn, EPS minus Rs 8.64. By segment: LPG operating profit Rs 2.11bn (profit after tax Rs 183mn), shipping loss Rs 2.52bn, trading loss Rs 1.08bn, property profit Rs 111mn.
Balance sheet, June 2026: borrowings Rs 36.9bn (Rs 20.3bn short-term), cash Rs 3.2bn, equity to owners minus Rs 1.92bn (minus Rs 4.97 a share).

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Sum of the parts less debt | 0.0 | 7.6 | 23.0 | 8.4
Recovery earnings × P/E | 0.0 | 5.0 | 24.0 | 7.3
Average | 0.0 | 6.3 | 23.5 | 7.9
Fair value about Rs 7.90 (30% bear, 50% base, 20% bull). Buy at up to Rs 6.70 (15% below); strong buy under Rs 5.90 (25% below).

Assumptions
LPG business worth 5 / 6.5 / 7 times operating cash profit of Rs 2.0 / 2.8 / 3.2bn (about Rs 3.1bn last year including depreciation, but only about Rs 390mn in April–June 2026). Ships and the Hambantota terminal (Rs 17.8bn of segment assets) at 50% / 80% / 90% of book. Investment property Rs 3.8 / 4.2 / 4.2bn. Net debt Rs 33.7bn. After a turnaround: EPS below zero / Rs 0.50 / Rs 2.00 at 10 / 12 times.

What stands out
- The LPG brand is a real business, but the group's debt is bigger than what all its parts are reasonably worth.
- Interest alone (Rs 2.8bn last year) is more than the group's operating profit.
- More than half the borrowings fall due within a year, so it depends on banks rolling them over.
- The market price looks like a bet on a rescue, a sale of the ships or a big recovery; none of that is announced in the reports.

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 7.90, 150 up to Rs 6.70, 150 up to Rs 5.90: average about Rs 6.94, about Rs 3,470 in total. That needs a fall of about 87%, so it isn't realistic. I'd wait until the debt is dealt with and look again.

What would change my view
Higher: selling or refinancing the ships, a rights issue or parent support that fixes equity, LPG margins holding after the 2026 price rises, shipping breaking even.
Lower: banks not rolling over short-term loans, more shipping losses, price controls on LPG, a dilutive rights issue.

Business tests: 0 of 4 passed: avoid for now.
